text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The mandate of the parliament will end tomorrow and the government will resign to allow for the formation of a new cabinet after parliamentary elections which ended last month.
-Amal Movement says that two of its fighters were killed in weekend clashes with Israeli forces near Yater just outside of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.

-Israel recognises its "mistake" in shelling civilians in south Lebanon on Saturday and the five-nation committee monitoring the Lebanon ceasefire agreement will meet today to discuss a Lebanese complaint over the incident.
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora says that the privatisation of investment sectors in Lebanon depends upon upgrading the administration, getting the best prices and providing the best services.
-Military court to look today into the case of eight people accused of spying for Israel.
-Maronite patriarch Sfeir says there will be no sovreignty, no integrity and no peace in Lebanon without giving the opposition the freedom of expression.
-Saudi Arabia will cover the medical expenses of a Palestinian man whose his son offered his own son for sale to cover his father's expenses.
-Cypriot economy minister held talks with his Lebanese counterpart.
